chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Whoever among you recognizes hardness in his heart, let him bring an orphan near and show him kindness, and let him wipe his head; his heart will soften by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the orphan has a right.”
And it is narrated that he said: “He should seat him at his table and wipe his head; his heart will soften.”

key_terms.حَقًّا: a right or due that must be acknowledged and fulfilled
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, in the sense of affectionately wiping the orphan’s head
key_terms.فَيُلَاطِفُهُ: then he shows him gentleness and kindness
key_terms.قَسَاوَةَ: hardness or harshness, here referring to spiritual hardness of heart
key_terms.قَلْبِهِ: his heart, meaning the inner spiritual and emotional state
key_terms.يَتِيمًا: an orphan, a child without a father and deserving special care

ai.seo_question: How does Islam teach a person to soften a hard heart?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that tenderness toward orphans is a means of softening the heart. It emphasizes the right of the orphan and encourages acts of kindness, nearness, and care as a moral remedy for spiritual hardness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.572 - The Messenger of Allah (sw) said:
"Whoever finds hardness in their heart should bring an orphan close, show kindness to them, and pass their hand over their head; this will soften their heart, by the permission of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, the orphan has a right."
It is also reported that He said: "He should seat the orphan at his table and pass his hand over their head, and this will soften his heart."
